stated: The Conservative Party will maintain the National Living Wage in each year of the next Parliament at two-thirds of median earnings, which is forecast to rise to around £13 per hour.

source.quote: We will maintain the National Living Wage in each year of the next Parliament at two-thirds of median earnings. On current forecasts, that would mean it rising to around £13 per hour...

bearing_set.reason: Maintaining the NLW at two-thirds of median earnings directly sets a wage floor affecting pay levels and security for lower-paid workers, earning a real verdict on good work & fair pay.
A rising wage floor increases take-home income for lower-paid households, with a plausible non-negligible effect on their ability to afford essentials — earning a real verdict on cost of living.

Linking the NLW to a fixed share of median earnings mechanically compresses the lower wage distribution and prevents the bottom from falling further behind the middle, producing a measurable effect on income inequality.

Mandated wage increases raise employer labour costs year-on-year, generating genuinely contested evidence on disemployment, hours reduction, and automation at the margin — a cross-outcome tradeoff that moves the 'economic opportunity' indicator in O13.

membership_note: Three bearings: O4 is the designed-for outcome; O14 captures the distributional compression effect (mechanistically distinct from O4's per-worker indicators); O13 captures the contested aggregate employment/opportunity tradeoff. O2 was considered but O4's in-work-poverty and real-wages indicators cover the relevant mechanism more precisely; O11 and O12 do not bear materially (this is a private-sector wage mandate, not a tax or direct spending commitment).
